previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including morbid obesity, polymyositis, interstitial lung disease, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and recurrent venous thromboembolism was admitted for painful, indurated skin lesions on her right leg and left arm that failed outpatient antibiotic therapy. Initial concern for cellulitis led to IV vancomycin, but biopsy confirmed panniculitis, likely triggered by recent acupuncture. Imaging revealed a small fluid collection in the left arm, but aspiration yielded no fluid; saline washout showed no organisms or white blood cells. She improved clinically and was transitioned to oral cephalexin and doxycycline. Concurrently, she was evaluated for bilateral eyelid swelling, with CT showing enlarged lacrimal glands and soft tissue masses, likely inflammatory; ophthalmology follow-up was arranged. Her INR was subtherapeutic, so she was bridged with fondaparinux and discharged on warfarin. She also experienced a single episode of mild diarrhea, which resolved and tested negative for C. difficile. She remained euvolemic, denied heart failure symptoms, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans.
